articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 2 Early Waiver Wire Pickups: Jalen Coker, Kaelon Black lead players to add
articles.summary: With fantasy football back in full swing, here are some early waiver wire pickups going into Week 2.
articles.body:
Fantasy football is back! Feels good. We're into Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season and the action was wild out the gate. We also already had a few games earlier in the week and have primetime to look forward to on Sunday and Monday nights. As always, we're going to be going over some early fantasy football waiver wire options going into Week 2 to help your lineups. Justin Boone will have a full look at the wavier wire on Tuesday.

Fantasy Football Waiver Wire: Week 2 Early Pickups

Jalen Coker, WR, Panthers (60% rostered)

Usually we like to stick to players who are rostered in under 50% of leagues but this number feels way too low for Coker given what he did on Sunday to the Bears. Apparently, some managers forgot about Coker's big performance last season in the playoffs in that near-upset versus the Rams (9-134-1).

Coker led the Panthers in pretty much all receiving categories against Chicago with eight catches on nine targets for 138 yards and two touchdowns, posting 29.8 fantasy points. Second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan, the presumed No. 1 for Carolina, was quiet for most of the game before getting to five catches on eight targets for 75 yards in garbage time (Coker also got a garbage-time score).

That won't be the case all season for McMillan, but clearly QB Bryce Young has built up a rapport with Coker despite the WR dealing with injuries the past few seasons. In 10-team leagues, Coker shouldn't be on the waiver wire and is worth adding given the Panthers next two opponents (@ ATL, @ CLE). Coker looks like a solid WR3/flex with WR2 upside after Week 1.

Kaelon Black, RB, 49ers (26% rostered on Yahoo)

The Niners defeated the Rams 27-7 in Australia on Thursday night and the backfield usage was one of the more intriguing storylines for San Francisco. We knew Kyle Shanahan would want to keep Christian McCaffrey fresh coming off a huge workload in 2025. But we didn't envision this type of split in Week 1 . Black won the backup RB gig out of camp and was expected to spell CMC on some downs — not nearly outproduce him to open the season.

McCaffrey had 36 snaps while Black played 28, and the rookie outcarried the vet 14-10. CMC still had a busy day in the passing game with five catches on eight targets for 20 yards, plus he was on the field in red-zone situations. But it's very clear Shanahan trusts Black to take some heat off CMC in an attempt to keep the superstar healthy. That's great news for both players, really. McCaffrey still got to 11.3 fantasy points in half-PPR while Black had 7.5.

If you have McCaffrey, you NEED to add Black in 12- or 14-team leagues. If the rookie back is hanging around the waiver wire, he's a top consideration give his current role and what his role would look like if CMC goes down with an injury. Looking ahead, the Niners have the Dolphins at home in Week 2, a great matchup for both backs. Black will maintain some flex value in deeper formats but is more of a stash play.

It was a funky game in Cincinnati as the Bengals took down the Bucs in Week 1. Three fumbles by Baker Mayfield led to Cincy jumping out to an early lead and coasting from there. One of those first-half scores was Gesicki, who finished with a surprising 5-78-1 line for 16.3 fantasy points.

Despite the lopsided result, the Bucs disrupted QB Joe Burrow enough where he had to go to his safety valve in Gesicky more often. WRs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for five catches on 10 targets for 71 yards, which isn't going to happen every week. But Gesicki isn't a stranger to solid fantasy results; he had three straight top-12 TE finishes from 2019-2021 with the Dolphins. Gesicki is a good add if you need a TE streamer in deep leagues, someone who should get looks in the red zone and is tied to an above-average offense.

If you're not into Gesicki, Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth (6%) had a solid line (5-46-1, 13.1 fantasy points) versus the Falcons. We know Aaron Rodgers may look Freiermuth's way a bit given his age.

Demarcus Robinson, WR, 49ers (0% rostered)

We're sticking with the 49ers for another recommendation, this time in the receiving corps. They lost rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling to injury on Thursday night and he's set to miss about a month with an ankle injury. San Francisco is already down Ricky Pearsall, and while George Kittle and Mike Evans are healthy right now, that can change quick.

Robinson is in his 11th season and has had spurts of productive play on some pretty good teams (Chiefs, Ravens, Rams) throughout his career. Robinson was huge for the 49ers in the wild-card round last season, posting a 6-111-1 line versus the Eagles. He only caught two of three targets on Thursday, but one was a 39-yard TD to help Robinson finish with 12 fantasy points.

The 49ers' next two opponents are the Dolphins and Cardinals — both soft matchups. Robinson was second among SF WRs in snaps (63%) versus the Rams and should start opposite Evans for the time being. Robinson is a strong add as a WR3/flex option in deeper PPR formats.

articles.title: Barella: ‘Going toe-to-toe with Real Madrid is what people expect from Inter’
articles.summary: Nicolo Barella says that Inter must look for the positives after tasting their first defeat of the season in the Champions League last week, but says that go...
articles.body:
Nicolo Barella says that Inter must look for the positives after tasting their first defeat of the season in the Champions League last week, but says that going toe-to-toe with Real Madrid at the Bernabeu is what people now expect from the Nerazzurri, which he thinks is a massive motivation.

Inter are back in Serie A action on Wednesday night at home against Udinese as Cristian Chivu and his players look to maintain their 100% win record at the start of the 2026-27 league campaign. Roma, who beat Torino on Monday night, are the only other side in the division with four wins from four in Serie A.

Barella reflects on Real Madrid and previews Inter vs. Udinese

MILAN, ITALY – APRIL 05: Nicolo Barella of FC Internazionale Milano celebrates scoring his team's fifth goal during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and AS Roma at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on April 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Barella stopped to speak to DAZN ahead of kick-off against Udinese in Serie A, and was asked for his opinions after a rare Inter defeat last week, away against Real Madrid in their 2026-27 Champions League opener.

"We've definitely done a lot of studying to understand what we can do better," said Barella (via TMW ).

"You always have to take something positive, even from defeats, and for us it is the fact that we had an open game at the Bernabeu against one of the best teams in the world. That's what people expect from us."

MADRID, SPAIN – SEPTEMBER 08: Vinicius Junior of Real Madrid is challenged by Andy Diouf of Internazionale during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Real Madrid C.F. and FC Internazionale Milano at Estadio Santiago Bernabeu on September 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

And how will Inter approach the rest of the Serie A campaign after tasting their first defeat of the season against Real Madrid?

"The season is a series of races. You have to be well focused on all the matches. Some might be more appealing, but they're all worth three points. We want to win, that's always been the case and always will be.

"We have the Scudetto on our shirts, we want to make life hard for those who want to take it away from us."

Barella was also asked for his thoughts on the increased level of competition in the Inter midfield this season. Hakan Calhanoglu is unavailable tonight, but the Italy international still has competition for playing time from the likes of Curtis Jones, Piotr Zielinski, Petar Sucic, Andy Diouf, Henrikh Mkhitaryan and Aleksandar Stankovic.

MADRID, SPAIN – SEPTEMBER 08: Curtis Jones of Internazionale is challenged by Dean Huijsen of Real Madrid during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Real Madrid C.F. and FC Internazionale Milano at Estadio Santiago Bernabeu on September 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

"I think it helps everyone to become better, it helps you stay on track and helps you to improve, which is the most important thing. We've brought in champions. They want to give us that extra step forwards, as well as wanting a new experience abroad.

"We're a strong team, we want to go all the way in all competitions."

articles.title: Bayern Munich Frauen earn hard fought 3-2 win in Leverkusen
articles.summary: If you poke the polar bear, you best be ready to pay for it.
articles.body:
It was not just the Männer who had to work for their win – Bayern Munich Frauen also made extremely hard work out of a rather scrappy game against Bayer Leverkusen.

The reigning champions were not helped by referee Anna-Lena Heidenreich, whose inconsistent calls were taken full advantage of by the hosts. A rather soft free kick from Paulina Tomasiak took a lucky deflection and looped out of Ena Mahmutovic 's reach for the opener.

That said, Bayern were not exactly in stellar form themselves, and while they were done harshly by the goal, one could argue they did not deserve to be leading at halftime. They did get an early equalizer in the second half, with Vanessa Gilles scoring her third goal in as many games through a well struck header. But injury returnee Franziska Kett made a poor pass that led to Tomasiak's second of the game soon after, and Bayern were chasing the game again.

Leverkusen turned the game more and more physical, with many players resorting to tucking the ball under their bodies to keep possession and draw fouls. However, said approach only took them so far, and substitute Edna Imade latched onto a Giulia Gwinn cross to head home the second equalizer.

At that point, the game was wide open, but Bayern were not going to settle for just a point. Indeed, with just two minutes left on the clock, Klara Bühl made a quick break and passed to another substitute in Alara, who deftly took a low driving shot that glanced off the post and into the net. For the first time in 88 minutes, Bayern were leading.

Stoppage time came and went, and despite a nervy moment or two, the champions saw out the win and maintained their winning streak.

Bayern's next game is a home Bundesliga meeting with FC Köln, and afterwards, the Bundesliga takes a short break as the Frauen begin their Champions League and DFB-Pokal campaigns.

Barcelona star Eric García has this week revealed his take that the podium for this year's Ballon d'Or award should be filled entirely by teammates from Hansi Flick's squad.

The subject of the upcoming 'Golden Ball' ceremony has of course dominated the headlines in Catalunya's capital over the course of the last week.

This comes owing not only to those Barcelona stars included on the 30-man shortlist, but also those left off.

Featuring front and centre were Blaugrana trio Lamine Yamal , Rodri and Pau Cubarsí , as well as the recently departed Ferran Torres . Surprisingly nowhere to be seen on the shortlist, though, were either Pedri or Raphinha .

Speaking during an interview with Cadena SER on Monday, the aforementioned Eric García was in turn asked for his take on the race to be named world football's best player for 2026.

And the former Manchester City man, as cited by El Chiringuito TV, went on to reveal his take that:

"The podium for the Ballon d'Or should be made up of players from Barca. And Lamine should win it!"

articles.title: Beatriz Álvarez sobre la Liga F: "Es el proyecto de mi vida"
articles.standfirst: La presidenta de la competición fue el rostro visible de la presentación de la competición para la temporada 26/27
articles.summary: La presidenta de la competición fue el rostro visible de la presentación de la competición para la temporada 26/27
articles.body: Aunque la Primera División femenina lleva ya tres jornadas disputadas, hoy se celebró la presentación de la competición para la edición 2026/2027. Una gala encabezada por la presidenta, Beatriz Álvarez, reelegida en el puesto este mismo año por los clubes. El evento, presentado por Susana Guasch, acogió futbolistas, como Noa Jiménez, del Madrid Club de Fútbol. Quinta temporada a nivel profesional. Una competición que cada año ha ido en aumento en todos los sentidos. También acudió José Manuel Rodríguez Uribe, el presidente del Consejo Superior de Deportes: "Hay cosas muy importantes aquí, valores, igualdad. Cada año veo más expectación. Diputados, senadores. Esto merece la pena. Fue una apuesta. Tuvimos aliados, pero también resistencia. Yo creo que la realidad nos ha dado la razón. Al principio se hacía por las jugadoras. Hacerlo profesional es reconocer derechos y avanzar en igualdad. Había que construir una competición y la presidenta a la cabeza lo hizo. La distancia entre clubes es cada vez menor. Hemos ayudado a construir la liga y también a los clubes". El presidente tiene claro lo necesario para que el fútbol femenino siga creciendo. "Hay que seguir apostando por el fútbol femenino y la Liga F. Esto se traduce en la selección española, campeonas del mundo. Me emociona ver a niños con camiseta de Aitana, Alexia. Es revolucionario", afirma. Una de las novedades este año para la liga es entrar en la quiniela. "Este miércoles vamos a hacer la presentación formal con los ministros. Es un tema importante para consolidar la Liga F y que siga creciendo. También hemos aprobado ayudas sociales y a la maternidad. Es todo un camino que tenemos por delante y la luz que tenemos al fondo nos sigue iluminando", añade José Manuel Rodríguez. Se acordaron de los clubes ascendidos este año a la máxima competición nacional, Alavés y Valencia. Una presentación que tuvo su parte de 'show', sacando a una futbolista de cada equipo para hacer un truco de magia. Tras ello, apareció la presidenta, Beatriz Álvarez. "Cuando empezamos teníamos una diapositiva de 'sin balones'. No había nada", comienza. "Dar las gracias a ministros, presidente del CSD, los patrocinadores, representantes institucionales de ligas, federaciones, a los clubes, a los medios porque sin vosotros sin dar protagonismo no tendría sentido, y a las protagonistas, las futbolistas. Os agradezco que hayáis hecho el esfuerzo por venir", agradecía. "Es el proyecto de mi vida. Tuvimos que atravesar muchas dificultades, pero lo que queda es ilusión y motivación", continuaba. Pero es proyecto de la máxima competición de fútbol femenino no se va a quedar ahí. "Afrontamos una nueva etapa que toca dar un salto. Esta es la quinta temporada. La última nos ha servido para levantar la mirada, planificar el futuro, la estrategia que tenemos que hacer, y la verdad es que todo se traduce en crecimiento. El objetivo era existir. Estamos liderando un movimiento que trasciende a muchas capas sociales. Sabemos que dos de las cosas que nos pueden hacer crecer son las asistencias y la experiencia de partido. Vivir el partido en familia, que el planazo sea el día de partido de Liga F, ese es el objetivo. Para que tengáis un dato, en la primera temporada de Liga F, abrimos ocho estadios principales y esta fueron 70. Creo que tiene que ir todo hacia ahí. El crecimiento comercial es fundamental para la sostenibilidad de lo clubes, visibilidad. Muchos retos y mucha ilusión", seguía. Las audiencias en la televisión de la liga han crecido un 127% desde la temporada 22/23. La campaña pasada, el clásico fue el partido más visto de la historia de la competición, más de 685 mil espectadores. Y no solo ha afectado a los partidos, si no también a su impacto digital. En las redes sociales, hubo más de 181 millones de visualizaciones, 20 veces más desde que se profesionalizó la competición, lo que ha llevado a tener 1,14 millones de seguidores y ser la liga del mundo en interacciones con sus seguidores. Los datos de las audiencias crecieron la pasada temporada, en parte gracias a combinar partidos cerrados y en abierto. "Era un objetivo que nos planteamos en el mes de febrero. Queríamos dar un paso mas y renegociamos con DAZN las condiciones para liberar partido en en abierto y tener mas visibilidad y un mayor impacto económico. Los datos nos avalan. En mayo se duplicaron los datos de audiencia media. Hemos apostado por esa 'doble v', de darle valor por un lado y por otro la visibilidad. Estamos trabajando de la mano de televisión española y TV3. Las dos primeras estamos muy contentos con las audiencias", dijo. Esta temporada, la liga femenina entra en la quiniela, un gran logro para el desarrollo de la competición. "Mas allá de hablar de crecimiento de la liga, es cierto que el fútbol femenino lidera algo más. Tenemos muchos proyectos. Por fin se da paso a quinielas, que es una tradición histórica. Se llevaba años persiguiendo y creo que al final se traduce en una normalización. No nos debemos olvidar de que trabajamos para que las niñas sueñen con ser futbolistas", señalaba. En 2022, se dio paso a la profesionalización de la liga. "Nosotros siempre lo defendimos. Crecer en ingresos para poder invertir y gastar mas. Lo que queremos es mejores condiciones para los futbolistas, pero también de infraestructuras. No todo es masa salarial. Lo que tenemos que hacer desde la liga y clubes generar ingresos. Tenemos que competir con ligas con modelo diferente. Entendemos que esos llevan riesgos. No creemos en ese modelo y lo que pretendemos es liderar esta etapa y dar mas derechos y condiciones a las futbolistas", continuaba. Durante muchos años, la liga se la ha llevado el Barcelona, aunque este año se le han ido piezas que pueden hacer que haya otro campeón. "La competitividad ha sido muy cuestionada desde el principio es el trabajo. No debemos lanzar este mensaje como algo catastrófico. Que se hayan ido no es un buena noticia, pero la liga y los cubes trabajan para generar continuamente referentes. Si se fijan en ellas es por los clubes y el trabajo que hay en España. Que lo valoren como una de las ligas referente y quieran quedarse". En la presentación estuvo Mauro Silva, vicepresidente de la Federación Paulista, y se acordó del club en el que estuvo y del buen momento que pasa ahora, el Deportivo de A Coruña. "Ganamos seis títulos. La gente vive muy intensamente el fútbol en A Coruña. Esto muy contento de cómo esta yendo. Fuerza Dépor", iniciaba. "Estuve muchos años aquí y cuando me marchó no había fútbol femenino. Venir años después y ver lo que es la Liga F me llena de ilusión. Nosotros en Sao Paulo también invertimos mucho en la liga femenina. Es garantizar que las niñas puedan soñar en jugar al fútbol. Desde la perspectiva de que una niña está en la grada de Riazor en el 92 y ahora esta misma niña ya tiene un objetivo dibujado me encanta. Es un proyecto que me ilusiona mucho y cuando conozco personas que están involucradas, me inspira más", contaba el exjugador. La entidad en la que es el segundo dirigente Mauro Silva ha llegado a un acuerdo con la Liga F. "Muchas veces se relaciona Sao Paulo con la ciudad. Pero en el estado somos 46 millones. Tenemos formación de futbolistas que después vienen a España y otros países de Europa. Formación, intercambio de experiencia, que profesionales de la Liga F puedan ir allí. Gente de allí que pueda venir a ver lo que está haciendo la Liga F. Me parece el mejor modelo. Nosotros no tenemos una liga profesional. Lo que hizo Liga F por nosotros nos apasiona y nos vale de inspiración. Ojalá algún día podamos llegar a este nivel", continuaba el brasileño. Según él, la mejor forma de hacer crecer la competición, es juntarse con gente que hace bien su labor. "La gente que trabaja en el deporte, ¿cómo mejora? Tu mejoras con gente al lado que es mejor que tú. También vale para las instituciones. Mejoras cuando trabajas con gente que lo hace tan bien como la Liga F. El próximo mundial es en Brasil y nos encantaría que una niña que lo vea y sueñe con jugar al fútbol, pueda hacerlo como lo ha hecho la Liga F. Ojalá estemos en la final Brasil y España", añadió el exfutbolista. "La liga allí se llama Paulista F, y ellos sí que son una verdadera inspiración, por la ilusión que tienen. Cuando estuvimos allí, las niñas dijeron a que se querían dedicar y la segunda profesión que mas salió era futbolista. Yo llevo una vida entera en el fútbol femenino e intento transmitir la esperanza", finalizó la presidenta. Por parte de Moeve acudió José María Solana. "Daros la enhorabuena a todos. Es un honor unirme a vosotros. Esto es evidente e imparable, un verdadero privilegio estar con vosotros. Nos pasa una cosa especial con la Liga F. Estamos muy identificados con ellos. Tenemos nuestra propia liga, queremos liderar en el sector energético, y tengo claro que ambos lo vamos a conseguir. El futuro es mejor si jugamos todos. Patrocinar la liga es un lujo", iniciaba. La Liga F también realizó el Torneo Liga Futura Moeve. "Esto es muy muy muy y me quedo corto, muy especial. Es maravilloso. Hablamos mucho de futuro. El futuro en Sevilla era una niña de 10 años que se puso las botas, la camiseta y salió a jugar al fútbol convencida de que si quiere puede ser futbolista. Tenemos que estar a la altura de la mirada de estas niñas", concluyó Solana. Para cerrar el acto acudió la ministra de igualdad, Ana Redondo. "Cuando las cosas no avanzan y van hacia atrás, es lo que hay que intentar evitar. Añadir ocho equipos a la quiniela cada semana, va a ser transformador. Va a ser revolucionario a nivel de públicos. Vamos a ver esos campos a rebosar. porque el fútbol femenino y la Liga F mueve muchas vidas y mucha ilusión para disfrutar del deporte y del fútbol. Va a transformar la vida de tantas niñas. En nuestro país los grandes avances han venido de la mano de la igualdad, del feminismo, de las mujeres que han decidido que no se nos pone nada por delante. Ha llegado a todos los rincones y por supuesto al fútbol, en un momento importante. El fútbol mueve ilusión, alegría, dinero también, pero es un deporte que va abriendo fronteras. La maternidad no puede ser un lastre. Por lo tanto, que hoy estemos aquí celebrando los triunfos y los avances, pero creo que no podemos quedarnos aquí. Si las futbolistas avanzan, el deporte avanza y España avanza. No podemos renunciar a anda, tenemos que seguir avanzando. Construyamos fútbol femenino, construyamos fútbol con mayúsculas", finalizó.

articles.title: What’s the VAR mistake controversy in Haaland’s Man City goal vs United?
articles.summary: Football players, fans, managers, and experts call for more accountability and less reliance on VAR for crucial calls.
articles.body:
The day after the Premier League’s Manchester derby, one of the biggest games in club football, the conversation is not dominated by the teams’ performances or players’ individual brilliance but by a controversial refereeing decision that allowed a seemingly offside goal to be overturned.

Erling Haaland’s controversially awarded goal for Manchester United in Sunday’s derby at Manchester United bagged his team three vital points and, more importantly, bragging rights over their rivals.

The result left thousands in the red half of Manchester feeling cheated and the plot thickened later in the day when the refereeing body revealed that the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) made the wrong call.

The 2026-27 Premier League season has barely completed its first month, but it is not wonder goals or last-minute saves making the headlines. Instead, VAR is the most hotly contested debate among fans, experts and managers who feel hard done by the use of technology.

Current and former United players, including club legend Wayne Rooney, labelled the use of VAR “horrendous”, while football experts told Al Jazeera the technology has become “far too dominant” in decision-making.

So how did we get here and what’s the fuss about VAR in the modern game? Al Jazeera Sport breaks it down:

VAR is a refereeing support tool designed to enable the checking, reviewing and correction of clear and obvious errors during a match, according to FIFA.

Football’s global governing body introduced the technology that is now used in over 300 competitions worldwide.

It was intended to be a combination of human expertise and technological accuracy, but has instead become a sour topic in football circles.

A dedicated team of video match officials (VARs) review decisions made by the on-field referee and speak directly with the match official via an audio communication system before a conclusion is reached.

First used in 2018-19, the VAR technology relies on video replays and reviews decisions related to four categories: goals, penalty decisions, direct red card incidents and mistaken identity.

What was the VAR controversy in the Manchester derby?

During the season’s first Manchester derby at Old Trafford, with City down to 10 players, striker Haaland scored in the 60th minute, slotting home at the back post from Josko Gvardiol’s cross.

The linesman initially disallowed the goal, suggesting Haaland was offside, but VAR overturned that decision, which caused controversy and left United fans furious.

While Haaland was played onside by Patrick Dorgu’s boot, his City teammate Enzo Fernandez, who dived to try to head the ball before Haaland, was in an offside position.

Replays showed Fernandez did not touch the ball, so the goal was given and it eventually proved to be the game-changer.

Premier League Match Centre posted on X after the goal to say the VAR “determined that Haaland was in an onside position” and “deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball”.

The refereeing body, Professional Game Referees (Pro Ref), admitted that the decision to allow Haaland’s goal was an “error of judgment”.

It said that VAR “did not recognise the likely impact” of Haaland’s teammate Fernandez, who attempted to head the ball from an offside position.

“The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position,” the statement said.

“In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective. However, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

“Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgment. A review of the incident will take place.”

Despite the wide-ranging criticism and repetitive errors, the use of technology is here to stay.

Al Jazeera has sought confirmation that VAR will continue to be used across all Premier League fixtures for the ongoing season and understands there will be no change.

Former United forward Rooney, who played for the Reds between 2004 and 2017, said the goal was “surely offside”, adding that Martinez was impacted by Fernandez’s movement.

“I am so sick of VAR,” Rooney said on the BBC’s Match Of The Day.

“It is horrendous; it takes all the emotion out of the game and to not see it… anyone who has played the game recognises he is offside. To get it so wrong is baffling.”

Gary Neville, former United captain who is a TV pundit for Sky Sports, said he expects a “massive inquest into the goal, which I think was wrongly given”. He added the decision left him so confused that he “needed the offside rule explained” to him.

Meanwhile, others have called for a “balance” in the use of VAR.

“VAR has become far too dominant in decision-making; the referee should be the primary decision-maker and should decide when he needs assistance with a call,” football presenter Joe Morrison told Al Jazeera.

He called for an increased use of pitch-side monitors by referees.

“He [referee] is out there in the middle, he is in the ‘zone’ and understands the context of what is happening around him instead of someone sitting remotely in a room in Stockley Park, West London,” said Morrison.

Should referees be held accountable for VAR errors?

Football expert Morrison thinks the best way of making VAR and referees more accountable for their controversial or incorrect calls is to make their decisions public.

“Both live on the field of play like rugby, and post-match. I would even start a post-match debrief with journalists as a matter of course,” he added.

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick was angry and baffled by the decision.

“I just don’t get it, I really don’t get it. I can’t understand how we’re trying to help referees, putting so many layers behind them, so many people, bodies and screens, and they can’t make the right decision,” Carrick told a post-match media conference.

Lisandro Martinez, the United defender at the centre of the controversy, said he was clearly impacted by the presence of his international teammate Fernandez and branded the goal an “injustice”.

“I went to him because he was in front of me. That’s why Haaland was free at the back,” Martinez told Sky Sports. “Five or six people [officials] doing this kind of mistake in the Premier League is unacceptable.

“We have to go home with this injustice.”

Yes. In the same match week, Arsenal conceded a penalty early in the second half of their 2-0 win over Sunderland after Ezri Konsa was penalised for wrestling Dan Ballard to the floor in the box.

Referee John Brooks awarded a penalty and the decision was checked and confirmed by VAR.

Although goalkeeper Raya went on to save Enzo Le Fee’s spot-kick, Arsenal boss Arteta was furious as pictures showed Ballard was also pulling Konsa as the pair fell to the ground inside the box. On Monday morning, British media reported Arsenal will contact Pro Ref over the incident.

“We have to go through what was done today that, in my opinion, is not acceptable,” said Arteta. “I watched it 20 times, and I cannot find a way to understand how they think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has not intervened.”

Earlier, questions were raised about VAR’s decision to allow Harry Maguire’s goal to stand in Man United’s 5-2 thrashing of Ipswich Town despite the ball coming off his arm, while manager Oliver Glasner said VAR should not have intervened to rule out a potentially match-winning goal from Neco Williams in Nottingham Forest’s 0-0 draw with Tottenham Hotspur.

When the Premier League introduced VAR in the 2019-2020 season, it said the reason was to curb mistakes that can change the outcome of a match, but seven years later, more than 75 percent of fans do not support the continued use of VAR, a survey by a football supporters group found in March.

The survey saw almost 8,000 fans of top-flight clubs participate and results showed that 75.7 percent did not support the use of VAR in football, with 91.7 percent saying VAR had removed the spontaneous joy of goal celebrations.

articles.title: César Tárrega sufre una lesión en la musculatura isquiosural de la pierna derecha
articles.standfirst: El futbolista pidió el cambio en la primera parte durante el partido contra el Sevilla
articles.summary: El futbolista pidió el cambio en la primera parte durante el partido contra el Sevilla
articles.body: El Valencia confirmó este lunes la lesión de César Tárrega, que sufre una lesión en la musculatura isquiosural derecha sufrida durante el encuentro disputado el pasado viernes ante el Sevilla, según el parte médico oficial. No por conocida, la baja de Tárrega deja de suponer un importante contratiempo para el equipo, si bien el próximo parón de Liga durante tres semanas, servirá para amortiguar la incidencia del período de ausencia. El defensa valenciano tuvo que abandonar el terreno de juego en el estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán durante la primera mitad, después de sentir molestias en la parte posterior del muslo derecho. El jugador pidió el cambio y fue sustituido por Iker Córdoba en torno al minuto 23 de partido. Todo apunta a que Tárrega ya había arrastrado molestias durante los días previos y que la lesión se produjo tras un sprint para evitar un ataque del Sevilla. Las pruebas médicas posteriores confirmaron la sospecha que se percibió en el terreno de juego con la afectación muscular en los isquiotibiales, aunque el club no facilita, como es costumbre, un plazo estimado de recuperación. La ausencia del central llega en uno de los momentos más delicados para la defensa valencianista. De hecho, el técnico interino Óscar Sánchez para el partido de este martes en Mendizorroza solo cuenta con el central Justin De Haas como jugador de ese puesto específico para ser alineado, si bien sale de una lesión, motivo por el que no sustituyó a Tárrega en el Pizjuán. Junto a él, la duda está en si ubica a Pepelu o mantiene al jugador del filial Iker Córdoba. Diakhaby y Copete continúan recuperándose de sus respectivas lesiones y habrá que esperar a después del parón internacional para ver en qué condiciones se encuentran.

articles.title: Este Eibar tiene mucha pólvora
articles.standfirst: Vendaval armero en Vigo • Ya ganaba 0-3 en el minuto 20 • Cuatro victorias seguidas, todas sin encajar goles • Mantiene plaza de ascenso directo
articles.summary: Vendaval armero en Vigo • Ya ganaba 0-3 en el minuto 20 • Cuatro victorias seguidas, todas sin encajar goles • Mantiene plaza de ascenso directo
articles.body: El Eibar no se quiere mover de los puestos de ascenso directo. En Balaídos realizó una exhibición. Fue una apisonadora y demostró máxima efectividad. Pasó por encima del Celta Fortuna, que por primera vez esta temporada sufrió de verdad lo que es jugar en una categoría como LaLiga Hypermotion. El conjunto de Jokin Arambarri recupera la segunda plaza y deja su portería a cero por cuarta jornada consecutiva, el mismo número de victorias que encadena. Y, además, iguala al Girona como equipo más realizador de la categoría (10 tantos cada uno). El partido no tuvo historia. A los 20 minutos estaba sentenciado, momento en el que el cuadro eibarrés ya dominaba por 0-3 con un Jon Guruzeta estelar, acompañado por Magunazelaia, que abrió el marcador con un gol soberbio, y Adu Ares. A partir de ese instante, el filial céltico lo intentó con más corazón que cabeza, pero la puntilla llegaría con el 0-4 al borde del descanso. El segundo tiempo fue prescindible. El filial mantuvo el tipo, intentando al menos el gol de la honra, que no llegó. Y el míster Fredi Álvarez fue expulsado al ver dos amarillas por protestar. Mientras, el Eibar vivió de rentas y Aranbarri movió el banquillo pensando en el siguiente partido. Incluso debutó Gift en los instantes finales. El trabajo ya se sido realizado en la primera parte. Al Fortuna, el encuentro le servirá para pisar tierra y aprender de errores, este lunes groseros en defensa, y darse cuenta de las dificultades de una categoría a la que acaba de llegar por primera vez en su historia.

articles.title: Leeds v Newcastle: How the players rated
articles.summary: How Leeds United and Newcastle United's players rated following their Premier League match.
articles.body:
Dominic Calvert-Lewin wreaked havoc as Leeds United moved up to third place in the Premier League table following a 4-1 win against Newcastle United at Elland Road.

Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

James Trafford: A relatively comfortable night against his former suitors. A couple of nervy clearances early on but went on to make an important save to deny Harvey Barnes. 7

James Justin: Teasing cross set up Leeds ' second goal. Has become a key component in this system. 7

Nico Elvedi: Only his second Premier League start yet already looks at home at Elland Road. Solid at the back but got it all wrong at the other end after volleying wide at the back post when unmarked. 7

Tarik Muharemovic: The club's player of the month for August for a reason. Made it look rather comfortable at the back on Monday night. 7

Jayden Bogle: Second goal credited to him. Did not know much about it, but has found his shooting boots after his goal at Brighton last time out in the league. Twice forced Lukas Hornicek into big saves before second goal took final touch off him. A real threat. 8

Anton Stach: Won a corner inside 32 seconds. That set the tone for Leeds ' relentless display, even if he later wasted chance to score. 7

Ethan Ampadu: Ensured Leeds kept pushing for more as he barked instructions. Saw Dominic Calvert-Lewin inadvertently block a vicious goalbound effort . 7

Ao Tanaka: His goal took two heavy deflections but had the confidence to take the shot. Looking back to his best in recent weeks even if he was relieved to see one misplaced pass unpunished. 7

Gabriel Gudmundsson: Caused Newcastle real problems with his runs down the left. Looked more a winger than a wing-back. 7

Noah Okafor: Fine strike for Leeds ' fourth, having also coolly pulled the ball back for Tanaka to let fly for his side's opener. 8

Dominic Calvert-Lewin: Just loves this fixture. A trademark header came off Bogle for Leeds ' second and then showed other side of his game to finish calmly on the floor for the hosts' third. Has scored eight goals against Newcastle - more than any other side. 9

Melvin Bard (on 72, Gudmundsson): Perfect environment to make his Premier League debut. 6

Brenden Aaronson (on 72, Tanaka): Lots of energy. 6

Harry Wilson (on 72, Okafor): Eager to impress. 6

Subs not used: Zetterer, Bijol, Bahoya, Nmecha

Lukas Hornicek: This would have been even uglier for the visitors were it not for Hornicek making fine saves to twice deny Bogle and also to foil Calvert-Lewin. 6

Amar Dedic: Shook off hamstring issue to start, but a tough night as Leeds repeatedly targeted his flank . 4

Malick Thiaw: Captain for night but this was far from a captain's performance. Beaten easily by Calvert-Lewin for Leeds ' second goal, slapped turf in frustration after the striker fired past him for the third and then failed to block Okafor's fourth. 3

Sven Botman: Like Thiaw, could not cope with Calvert-Lewin and was skinned so easily for Leeds ' second goal. 3

Lewis Hall: Dragged out of position in build-up of Leeds ' second goal. Not the night he had in mind after signing a new deal. 4

Nico Gonzalez: Belatedly came off after just 19 minutes after the ball struck him in the head in the early stages. 5

Lewis Miley: Little he could do for deflection for Tanaka's goal, but was overrawed by Leeds ' tenacious midfield. Had little time to find passing rhythm. 4

Jacob Murphy: Continued in injured Anthony Elanga's absence, but did not offer enough protection and caused Leeds few problems going the other way. 3

Yoane Wissa: Created Newcastle 's best chance and at least battled and chased, even if his final ball was not always great. 5

Harvey Barnes: Has a fearsome record against Leeds and eyes lit up when he danced inside the box only for Trafford to deny him. 5

Matias Fernandez-Pardo: Full debut following his £51.4m move from Lille. Had little to feed off as Newcastle repeatedly played long balls forward. 4

Sean Steur (on 19, Gonzalez): Thrown into the cauldron after Gonzalez went off. Could do little about deflection before Leeds ' first goal but gave the ball away in build up to Leeds ' second. Eighteen-year-old will learn from experience. 4

Bazoumana Toure (on 58, Murphy) So rapid and pulled one back. Bright cameo as he pushes for a start. 6

Joe Willock (on 58, Fernandez-Pardo): One decent chance landed on roof of net from tight angle. 5

Tino Livramento (on 58, Dedic): Another step on return from injury. Set up Toure's consolation. 6

Aladji Bamba (on 79, Miley): A rare sighting following his summer move from Monaco. 5

Subs not used: Pope, Schar, Ramsey, M.Miley

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: Un Betis exuberante hurga en la herida del 'submarino'
articles.standfirst: Los verdiblancos ganan 1-2 al Villarreal en La Cerámica en un duelo en el que pudieron golear
articles.summary: Los verdiblancos ganan 1-2 al Villarreal en La Cerámica en un duelo en el que pudieron golear
articles.body: Un Betis exuberante, que remató más de 20 veces y perdonó lo que podría haber sido una goleada de escándalo, se ha llevado los tres puntos de su visita al Estadio de La Cerámica. Los de Pellegrini, que se pusieron por debajo en el marcador poco antes de la media hora, remontaron en dos zarpazos antes del descanso y en la segunda mitad perdonaron una infinidad de ocasiones ante un Gulácsi que evitó el bochorno, pero no pudo evitar que los verdiblancos hurgaran en la herida de un proyecto, el de Iñigo Pérez, que ha comenzado torcido. El conjunto verdiblanco completa su tres de tres: victoria en Liga ante el Real Madrid, triunfo ante el Lille en Francia en su estreno en la Champions y golpe sobre la mesa ante uno de sus rivales directos en la lucha por los puestos europeos. Doce puntos de quince posibles para un Betis que pone tierra de por medio con el 'submarino'. Los amarillos siguen sin ganar este curso y apenas suman dos puntos en la competición doméstica. Para colmo, cayeron en Dortmund en la Champions, y su afición está ya de uñas... El arranque del partido respondió a las expectativas que generan dos de los equipos que mejor juegan de LaLiga. El Villarreal salió dispuesto a imponer un ritmo altísimo, con una presión adelantada muy intensa y mayor dominio del balón frente a un Betis ordenado atrás y preparado para salir con velocidad. Pellegrini dio descanso a Antony y apostó por un doble pivote mixto, con Marc Roca como futbolista más posicional y Fornals aportando creatividad. Pépé firmó el primer disparo, pero las ocasiones de verdad no tardaron en llegar y el encuentro se convirtió pronto en un intercambio de golpes... En apenas unos minutos pudo pasar de todo. Bellerín, tras un córner de Isco y un primer remate rechazado, se encontró con un paradón de Gulácsi a su segundo intento. Respondió inmediatamente el Villarreal aprovechando un error de Bartra: Gerard Moreno asistió a Comesaña, Valles sacó su remate con el hombro, el balón golpeó en el larguero y el guardameta volvió a intervenir ante Buchanan. Poco después, Gerard vio cómo no subía al marcador un gol suyo por un claro fuera de juego y Fornals desperdició una gran oportunidad tras una magnífica combinación entre Abde, Isco y Bellerín. El encuentro se abrió por completo, con los dos equipos cargando el área y buscando la portería contraria sin demasiados rodeos. La defensa verdiblanca tiraba con precisión la línea del fuera de juego y dejó varias veces adelantados a los atacantes locales. Así ocurrió de nuevo cuando Buchanan culminó con un gran zurdazo una acción iniciada por Carlos Romero con un bonito pase con el exterior, con el VAR confirmando que el canadiense estaba ligerísimamente adelantado y anulando el que habría sido el primer tanto de la noche. Justo antes de la media hora, el Villarreal terminó encontrando el 1-0 en una acción de estrategia. Después de avisar con un córner sacado en corto que terminó con un remate de Mikautadze despejado por Valles, los amarillos repitieron la fórmula. Pape Gueye puso el centro al segundo palo, Isco rompió esta vez la línea del fuera de juego, Renato Veiga ganó el balón por arriba y Gerard Moreno apareció para rematar de volea a la red. El gol, sin embargo, lejos de descomponer al Betis, provocó la mejor reacción de los de Pellegrini. Sólo un minuto después, Fran García alcanzó la línea de fondo y puso un magnífico balón para que el Cucho cabeceara obligando a Gulácsi a realizar otra gran parada. Abde e Isco comenzaron a encontrar espacios y el Betis encerró por momentos al Villarreal. Camino del 40', Isco construyó la jugada del empate con una acción extraordinaria desde el centro del campo, dejando atrás a dos rivales antes de encontrar a Abde. El marroquí se deshizo de Mouriño con el control, superó después a Pépé y remató raso. Gulácsi consiguió detener su disparo, pero el Cucho, atento al rechace, apareció para empujar con la izquierda a la red. El Betis no levantó el pie del acelerador y terminó convirtiendo su reacción en remontada antes del descanso. Una buena salida desde atrás iniciada por Fornals terminó con Isco recortando hacia dentro y buscando portería. Su disparo rozó en un defensa y se marchó a córner. El propio capitán se encargó de ponerlo en juego, Abde prolongó en el primer palo y Gulácsi metió la mano abajo para impedir que Riquelme rematara. La pelota quedó suelta y Natan, completamente solo, la recogió para colocar el 1-2 junto al palo más alejado. En apenas un cuarto de hora, los verdiblancos habían dado la vuelta a un partido frenético en el que los dos porteros habían tenido que multiplicarse. El intercambio de golpes continuó tras el descanso. Buchanan probó fortuna con un golpeo seco que se marchó fuera y el Betis respondió con una buena combinación entre Fornals, Cucho, Isco y Abde que terminó con un remate de Riquelme desviado a córner por la defensa. Mucho más clara fue la siguiente. Abde firmó un jugadón por la izquierda, dejando atrás a Mouriño y Pau antes de servir atrás para el Cucho, que remató a bocajarro y se encontró con una extraordinaria parada con el pie de Gulácsi cuando ya se cantaba el tercero. El Villarreal buscó una reacción desde el banquillo con las entradas de Moleiro y Saliba, mientras Pellegrini dio los primeros minutos de la temporada a Ceballos sustituyendo a Isco. Moleiro avisó nada más entrar con una diagonal desde la izquierda y un disparo al palo largo que se marchó fuera. Los amarillos adelantaron metros y consiguieron instalarse durante varios minutos en campo contrario ante un Betis cada vez más replegado y que perdía demasiado rápido la pelota. Mikautadze encontró un hueco en el área para controlar, girarse y probar con un remate raso que atrapó Valles. Pero llegó la reacción desde el banquillo. Pellegrini dio entrada a Antony y Deossa y el partido cambió de escenario. El Villarreal siguió obligado a adelantar líneas, pero el Betis encontró de repente autopistas para correr. Deossa fue el gran agitador. Primero irrumpió por la izquierda y puso un balón perfecto a Fornals, completamente solo en el punto de penalti, pero el mal control del castellonense le impidió siquiera rematar. Poco después, el colombiano protagonizó otra conducción portentosa, esta vez por la derecha, se plantó en el área y soltó un zurdazo que volvió a encontrarse con el guardameta local. El Betis alternaba el bloque bajo para cerrar espacios con salidas vertiginosas cada vez que recuperaba. Ceballos dejó buenos minutos en su regreso, dando agilidad a la circulación y aportando también un par de recuperaciones importantes. Los verdiblancos, cargados de futbolistas de enorme calidad técnica en la medular, mostraron por momentos una facilidad extraordinaria para mover la pelota, escapar de la presión y convertir una recuperación en una transición peligrosa con apenas unos pases. El Villarreal trató de cambiar de nuevo el partido con Freeman y Ayoze, pero cada paso adelante multiplicaba los espacios a su espalda. Antony se quedó completamente solo ante Gulácsi y el portero húngaro volvió a sacar abajo un remate que parecía destinado al 1-3. Poco después, el Betis salió de maravilla desde atrás y fue el Cucho quien se plantó en el área, aunque su disparo cruzado se marchó rozando el palo. El equipo de Pellegrini perdonaba una sentencia tras otra mientras Gulácsi, pese a la derrota, sostenía al Villarreal con una colección de grandes paradas. Los locales aún encontraron fuerzas para responder. Moleiro vio cómo la defensa desviaba a córner un remate tras un pase de Oluwaseyi y, en el saque de esquina, Mikautadze cabeceó en el segundo palo a las manos de Valles. Pero el verdadero peligro seguía apareciendo al otro lado. Deossa, ya ejerciendo como falso nueve, volvió a recorrer medio campo a base de potencia antes de cruzar demasiado su disparo y poco después soltó un zapatazo monumental con la zurda desde fuera del área que Gulácsi despejó a una mano. El recital de ocasiones verdiblancas todavía tuvo un último capítulo. Con un Betis que superaba ya los 20 remates, más de una decena entre los tres palos, Bellerín tiró una pared con un exuberante Deossa en el centro del campo y se encontró completamente solo para correr hacia la portería. El lateral llegó hasta el área y buscó el remate por abajo, pero otra vez apareció Gulácsi. El portero húngaro evitó que el marcador reflejara la enorme superioridad del Betis en las transiciones y mantuvo hasta el final un 1-2 que se quedó muy corto para todo lo que perdonaron los de Pellegrini.

articles.title: Scotland: Luke Graham & Robbie Ure in Pocognoli's first squad
articles.summary: Stoke City centre-half Luke Graham and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure will receive their first full Scotland call-ups on Tuesday when Sebastien Pocognoli names his first squad as head coach.
articles.body:
Stoke City centre-half Luke Graham and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure will receive their first full Scotland call-ups on Tuesday when Sebastien Pocognoli names his first squad as head coach.

Graham was part of Scotland's pre-World Cup training camp in May after a breakthrough campaign with Dundee, winning the Scottish Premiership club's players' player and young player of the year awards.

The 22-year-old was an unused substitute in the country's send-off friendly win against Curacao, which was also Steve Clarke's last game in the dugout at Hampden Park.

The defender, who has three caps at under-21 level, has started strongly for The Potters in the Championship, who are unbeaten in their last four games, with Graham an ever-present.

Former Rangers academy product Ure was in demand across Europe after a free-scoring spell - 20 goals and three assists in 20 matches - that took Sirius to the top of the table in Sweden and it resulted in a £5.5m summer transfer to La Liga with Sevilla.

Time for Pocognoli to pick - who could be named in new-look Scotland squad?

Stoke best place for me to take step up - Graham

Is Sevilla's 'all-round striker' Ure ready to lead Scotland's attack?

Ure, also 22, has yet to find the target in Spain, but given his eligibility for Ukraine, the new head coach appears tempted to tie him down as soon as possible as he is set to be named in the Belgian's squad when it will be announced at 11:00 (BST).

Since Poconogli was announced as Clarke's successor - after the former Kilmarnock manager resigned after the Scots failed to qualify for the knockout stages of a major tournament for the first time - the expectation has been that the Belgian will look to freshen up an ageing squad.

His countryman, Heart of Midlothian head coach Wouter Vrancken, is "confident" there will also be a few players from the Gorgie club included.

His front three of striker James Wilson and wingers Calvin Miller and Josh McPake have been receiving plaudits for their recent performances.

Former Scotland captain Scott Brown too has high hopes for the Hearts wingers who have heavily contributed to their side's strong start to the season.

Pocognoli will take charge of Scotland for the first time on Saturday, 26 September in the Scots' Nations League B opener against Slovenia and his debut in the Hampden dugout will be three days later against Switzerland.

articles.title: El Villarreal iguala su peor inicio defensivo en Primera
articles.standfirst: Los diez tantos recibidos en las cinco primeras jornadas igualan el registro histórico de la 2023-24
articles.summary: Los diez tantos recibidos en las cinco primeras jornadas igualan el registro histórico de la 2023-24
articles.body: El Villarreal no levanta cabeza en este inicio de temporada y sus números defensivos tienen gran culpa de ello. Con los tantos encajados ante el Betis el equipo amarillo ha igualado su peor inicio defensivo en Primera división después de sumar dos goles más en contra. El conjunto amarillo suma ya 10 tantos recibidos en las cinco primeras jornadas de LaLiga. El equipo entrenado por Iñigo había llegado a la cita ante el conjunto verdiblanco con ocho goles encajados en las cuatro primeras jornadas. Los dos tantos del Betis elevan ahora la cifra hasta los diez, situando al Villarreal en un registro que no alcanzaba desde 2023-24, cuando también recibió diez goles en sus cinco primeros encuentros. Y en esta ocasión, tan sólo la actuación del guardameta Gulacsi, que detuvo varios mano a mano claros en la segunda mitad, impidió que la estadística fuese todavía peor. El arranque defensivo está muy lejos de los mejores registros del conjunto castellonense. Un agujero que está lastrando sobremanera a los castellonenses, que todavía no conocen la victoria con el técnico navarro en el banquillo y que ven cómo les condena a la zona de descenso

articles.title: Pellegrini: "No es fácil crearle esta cantidad de ocasiones a un equipo como el Villarreal aquí en su casa"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Betis, muy satisfecho tras la victoria de su equipo por 1-2 en La Cerámica
articles.summary: El técnico del Betis, muy satisfecho tras la victoria de su equipo por 1-2 en La Cerámica
articles.body: Manuel Pellegrini, técnico del Betis, se mostró muy satisfecho tanto por el espectáculo ofrecido por los dos equipos esta noche en La Cerámica como, sobre todo, por el rendimiento ofrecido por sus futbolistas, remontando un marcador adverso frente al Villarreal, uno de sus rivales directos en LaLiga, para sumar tres puntos en el primero de sus tres compromisos de esta semana. Valoración del partido: "En general fue un partidazo. Me alegro mucho porque el fútbol es un espectáculo y creo que son dos equipos que saben jugar y buscar la portería contraria. Hicimos un partido muy completo; quizás nos faltó tener un poco más de tranquilidad en las cuatro o cinco ocasiones de gol muy claras que tuvimos en el segundo tiempo como para haber liquidado el partido. No las convertimos, pero seguimos intentando buscar la portería con seguridad defensiva, por lo que ante un muy buen equipo en su casa me dejó muy contento lo que hizo el equipo". Gestión de la ventaja y nervios finales: "Por supuesto que sí. Cuando uno está solamente con un gol de diferencia y falla tantos goles, por lo general el fútbol te castiga y viene el empate. Creo que estuvimos atentos defensivamente y seguimos siempre buscando la portería contraria, aunque un poco acelerados e imprecisos en las definiciones. No es fácil crearle esta cantidad de ocasiones a un equipo como el Villarreal aquí en su casa. En términos generales me dejó muy contento, sobre todo porque no se le dieron opciones al Villarreal de hacer daño y no crearon prácticamente ninguna, especialmente en la segunda parte. Tuvieron un par de llegadas peligrosas en la primera parte, pero en la segunda tuvieron menos; el mismo hecho de estar en desventaja los obligó a dejar más espacio y lo supimos aprovechar bien". Arranque de curso y calendario: "Es muy importante partir con victoria en los primeros partidos. Después hay una intensa Champions League todas las mitades de semana y nos quedan todavía seis puntos más antes de ir al primer parón. Tenemos que intentar seguir sumando, pero con el convencimiento de que lo que hemos hecho en estos partidos para ganar no nos va a servir por sí solo para ganar el próximo. Si repetimos lo que estamos haciendo sí, pero creo que no hay que confiarse; hay que saber que todos los equipos son muy complicados y ahora tenemos que intentar sumar tres puntos en casa". Una plantilla de talento: "Así es. Tenemos muchos jugadores muy creativos: no solamente están ellos dos, también está Fidalgo que juega muy bien, después está Gio Lo Celso, Ceballos e Isco. Tenemos jugadores creativos porque este equipo trata de jugar creativamente y buscar siempre la portería contraria. Hay muchísimos partidos, así que mientras haya un grupo comprometido con un proyecto, creo que tenemos que seguir avanzando".

articles.title: Cucho Hernández: "La seguridad defensiva fue enorme contra jugadores de mucha calidad"
articles.standfirst: El colombiano además lamenta las ocasiones falladas pese a la victoria en La Cerámica
articles.summary: El colombiano además lamenta las ocasiones falladas pese a la victoria en La Cerámica
articles.body: El Cucho Hernández, autor del primero de los dos goles del Betis en La Cerámica frente al Villarreal, fue el encargado de analizar en los micrófonos de Movistar LaLiga el triunfo de los verdiblancos frente al equipo de Iñigo Pérez. El colombiano volvía a la titularidad después de descansar entre semana en la Champions League y aprovechó la oportunidad estrenando su cuenta realizadora en esta Liga. El Betis pudo golear: "Sí, yo creo que la autoexigencia que tiene este equipo no se permite irse tan contento esta noche porque es verdad que enfrentamos a un Villarreal que siempre es un rival directo por la pelea de Europa, pero también que tuvimos tres o cuatro muy claras. Yo en lo personal tuve dos que tienen que ser gol, pero lo importante es hacer crítica, mejorar y corregir desde la victoria, que es lo mejor que te puede pasar. Así que seguimos". La clave del triunfo: "Pues yo creo que hay que darle mucho mérito a la defensa. La seguridad defensiva el día de hoy fue enorme contra jugadores de mucha calidad que tienen ellos arriba. Prácticamente no nos crearon peligro en la segunda parte. Nosotros pudimos darle un regalo de una ventaja a nuestros defensores, pero a veces estas cosas pasan. Lo importante es pensar en el siguiente, mejorar y sumar tres puntos más, que es un camino casi perfecto hasta ahora". El Betis, con números para estar arriba: "Sí, con calma, obviamente, pero con mucha ilusión de que la gente se ilusione con este equipo. Vendrán momentos difíciles, pero creo que la unión, la honestidad y el trabajo no se reemplazan aquí, así que seguiremos por este camino".

articles.title: Iñigo Pérez: "No estoy dando el nivel"
articles.standfirst: El Villarreal sigue sin ganar esta temporada y su técnico se muestra autocrítico con su gestión
articles.summary: El Villarreal sigue sin ganar esta temporada y su técnico se muestra autocrítico con su gestión
articles.body: El Villarreal sigue sin carburar. Aún no ha ganado en LaLiga ni en Champions y las alarmas comienzan a sonar en La Cerámica. Iñigo Pérez asumió toda la responsabilidad tras la derrota del Villarreal ante el Betis en el Estadio de la Cerámica. El técnico se mostró autocrítico ante un inicio de temporada complicado que deja al equipo en puestos de descenso. Explicación: “Si tuviese explicación, le pondría remedio. No estoy dando con el nivel. Insistiré hasta que surja. No sé si es ansiedad, temor o impotencia. Hay que reflexionar seriamente sobre el estado en que estamos como grupo y tomar decisiones”. Imagen tras el descanso: “La segunda parte es dañina. Tanto para nuestra autoestima como para nuestra confianza. Para todo aquello que habíamos cimentado y esas cosas a las que podíamos agarrarnos. Nos hace daño esta sensación que genera la segunda parte; levantarse desde ahí es muy complicado, pero hay que hacerlo. Hoy no puedo rescatar nada”. Intranquilidad en el vestuario: “La preocupación siempre existe; queremos generar cualquier situación, por pequeña que sea. Pero ahora estamos hablando de momento de acciones con gran peso e importancia en los resultados. Como entrenador no puede faltar a la verdad y eludir la responsabilidad de lo que está sucediendo”. Responsabilidad del entrenador: "Creo que es falta de capacidad del entrenador. Ahí es donde tengo que incidir. Mirarme a mí mismo y ver qué puedo hacer para que esto cambie". Estado del equipo:·"No hay que poner paños calientes. Treinta minutos después del partido, no existe una ilusión para lo que viene. Mañana seguro que sí, pero ahora no. El pensamiento positivo, que tan de moda está, no nos ayuda. Ahora mismo estamos mal".

articles.title: Leeds 4-1 Newcastle: Matthias Jaissle handed first defeat as Magpies boss as Dominic Calvert-Lewin leads Elland Road rout
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Leeds defeat Newcastle 4-1 in the Premier League; Dominic Calvert-Lewin was the star of the show as Leeds move up to third in the  table; defeat is the first for Matthias Jaissle as Newcastle boss
articles.body:
Both sides came into the game with five points on the board from the opening three games, but Matthias Jaissle's bubble was emphatically burst as he suffered a dramatic first defeat as Newcastle boss.

Without the electric Anthony Elanga, the visitors offered much less of a threat and could not handle the relentless press from the home side, led by the imperious Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Latest news and rumours: Leeds | Newcastle

Leeds felt slighted when Matias Fernandez-Pardo, making his first start for his new club, avoided punishment for an alleged 'handball' inside the penalty area. That was soon forgotten as the hosts' dominance soon paid off.

There was an element of luck to their first, as Ao Tanaka's shot deflected off two Newcastle defenders with the last touch coming off Lewis Miley to wrong-foot Lukas Hornicek.

That then led to the Calvert-Lewin show truly beginning. The striker thought he had his eighth career goal against the Magpies with a bullet header three minutes later. However, replays showed the ball had last come off team-mate Jayden Bogle, meaning he had to settle for the assist.

The Leeds No 9 wasn't to be denied his next goal, bulldozing his way into the penalty area before calmly slotting home a third before the break.

The floodgates remained firmly open after half-time, with Noah Okafor adding a fourth - and the pick of the bunch. The forward produced a delightful weak-foot volley on the bounce, sending it arrowing into the bottom corner.

Bazoumana Toure grabbed a late consolation, but it did little to take the gloss off a thoroughly one-sided display. The result leaves Leeds sitting third at the end of the fourth round of fixtures - their highest position at this stage of a season since the 2000/01 campaign.

2: NO PENALTY! Fernandez-Pardo avoids conceding spot-kick for alleged ‘handball.’

14: SAVE! Hornicek makes a top drawer save from close range to deny Bogle.

25: SAVE! Bogle again threatens as he stings the palms of Hornicek with vicious attempt.

32: GOAL! Tanaka’s deflected strike comes off TWO Newcastle players before beating Hornicek.

35: GOAL! Two in three minutes as Bogle gets last touch from Calvert-Lewin's bullet header.

41: SAVE! Best chance of the half for Newcastle as Barnes is denied from close range.

45+1: GOAL! Calvert-Lewin can’t be stopped as he finally gets his goal.

59: GOAL! Okafor gets in on the act with stunning strike on the bounce.

89: GOAL! No clean sheet for Leeds as Toure adds late consolation.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke speaking with Sky Sports:

“I wasn’t happy that we allowed them to score one goal. But, it doesn’t take anything away from the fact that my boys were brilliant and we fully deserved to win the game. There’s no such thing as a perfect performance though, and this is one of the rare points I have to criticise.

“We have energy, quality, good structure in and out of possession. We have a good fitness level, also. It’s not just the will, otherwise whoever had the strong will would always win the game. We have to have the right triggers and everyone needs to be spot on. It’s lots of work on the training ground to be that compact and intense.

“He’s in outstanding shape and he plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group and he’s taken the responsibility.

“His work rate is top. It’s not just scoring the goals. The way he plays for us is outstanding. He’s definitely one of the stand out strikers in the league.”

Jaissle: We didn't match Leeds physically

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle speaking with Sky Sports:

"That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said many times we will have ups and downs and challenges along the way. Tonight, we faced that challenge. It’s really tough. Difficult to digest, but this is a chance to learn because there’s not long until the next match at home to show the right reaction.

"You need to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against a physical and strong team. Leeds are so intense, especially at home and we couldn’t match that physicality in the first half. That was a key element. No excuses, we have to learn from it.

"Injuries are also a challenge that we need to overcome and will. This is the message I have given to the players. There will be no issue with confidence."

Jamie Carragher on Monday Night Football:

"Leeds are fifth in the Premier League table since December. That should make Newcastle feel better as it has been a bad night for them when the world was watching. They have been beaten up by a really good Premier League team.

"It will be a tough season at times for Newcastle with the manager and young players finding their feet in the Premier League. They just got beaten up."

"Calvert-Lewin was unplayable. One of the greatest sights in football is seeing a centre-forward rise above everyone and attack the ball.

"Look how high his legs are. I don't think there is a better player in the air in the Premier League."

"That has to be a huge learning curve for Newcastle tonight. Looking at the team sheet for that opening game against Liverpool, with a midfield two and Yoane Wissa in the No 10, it looked like they were going to get overpowered.

"They didn't. Perhaps it was the emotion of the Kevin Keegan tributes, maybe it was because it was the opening game, or perhaps it was the Alexander Isak motivation. There was a lot going on that day.

"But Leeds away on a Monday night, you need physicality & runners. Even a midfield three of Bruno Guimaraes-Sandro Tonali-Joelinton would find that a tough match tonight.

"Newcastle were bullied by Leeds' physicality and numerical advantage in the engine room.

"It's a long season, and it's been a very good start, but that's a real eye opener for the the new Newcastle manager."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Troy Deeney's Team of the Week: Donnarumma, Konsa, Fernandez, Schade
articles.summary: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?
articles.body:
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

Gianluigi Donnarumma ( Manchester City ): Not only is he one of the best goalkeepers in the world, but he is a big-match player. We've seen it year on year and he's just won Manchester City two extra points against Manchester United . He'll get them 10 points over the course of the season, he's that good. After the Community Shield, people were saying he wasn't good enough and they should have kept James Trafford, but he proved again why he's such a big-time goalkeeper.

Daniel Munoz ( Nottingham Forest ): I thought he was a breath of fresh air in the win at Villa . No-one in that Forest team can do what he does. Pace, power, he can defend and offers you a lot going forward. I thought he was a steal. I can't believe Liverpool and Manchester United didn't go for him. Forest did unbelievable business getting him.

Ezri Konsa ( Arsenal ): Had a tough old battle against Brian Brobbey as they beat Sunderland . Last season, he ended up bullying Gabriel for the equaliser and he wanted no part of it. Konsa said 'no problem' and stepped up. That penalty was never a penalty.

Lewis Dunk ( Brighton ): Who knew the big 6ft 5in centre-half could put one in to the top bins, straight off the crossbar? Unbelievable. He goes in just for that strike against Coventry alone.

Tarik Muharemovic ( Leeds United ): What a beast he is. I don't know where Leeds found him but he heads it, kicks it, runs through people. Didn't get the clean sheet against Newcastle but deserved it.

Leif Davis ( Ipswich Town ): Very, very good. Very underrated. He delivered in a six-pointer because I think Palace are going to be down there, with a goal and an assist.

Enzo Fernandez ( Manchester City ): He had his best game in the last two years against Manchester United . He actually did everything the team needed - ran with the ball, looked after it, bought fouls, tried his best to get others sent off. I thought he was a catalyst for the team. His best performance for City so far.

Pascal Gross ( Brighton ): Goal and assists. The old head who they brought back steadies that ship - it's a really young team. He is even more important now with no Welbeck, no Milner. He is in and is a steady hand.

Kevin Schade ( Brentford ): Two goals again at Bournemouth . I feel like he's the next one they'll sell. Pace, power, scores goals and works hard for the team.

Mohamed Belloumi ( Hull City ): Was decent in the Championship but he's really taken to the Premier League. Looks like he's stepped up and thought he'll have a bit of this. Two goals away at Chelsea is huge. They probably felt like they should have won.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin ( Leeds United ): Steady away, isn't he? Goes about his business. Got one goal against Newcastle , should have had two. Excellent as a forward. Leeds have done something to keep him fit and he's changed the mentality for sticking in there. Maybe it's the Elland Road factor. They won't allow for anyone to not give 100%. He stays in the game all the time.

Enzo Maresca ( Manchester City ): An honourable mention for Mikel Arteta. Got the job done away again. We could have had Daniel Farke. We'll give it to Maresca. I'm not his biggest fan, but tactically he got it right at Old Trafford. He understood the moment and gave his team the best platform to do what they needed to win. Made a brave call in bringing Cherki off for Ndiaye.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin can't have it both ways: Either own the ugly Ole Miss exit, or stop trying to rewrite history
articles.summary: Kiffin stiff-arming Ole Miss for LSU is one thing, but his re-imagining of the whole saga is another. He is the villain in this rivalry story, even if he can...
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin has been through so many lifetimes in college football and tried on so many different versions of himself that sometimes you wonder if he gets confused about which character he's supposed to play.

When Kiffin left Ole Miss last December for LSU , sacrificing a viable chance to win last year's national championship in the process, he did it for a defensible reason. Though everything about the timing and execution was terrible, there was nothing controversial about the belief he'd have a better chance of consistently contending for titles at LSU.

Kiffin held a news conference in Baton Rouge on Monday to kick off the week all of college football has been waiting for since he changed jobs. Though the game itself is among the best all year, with real College Football Playoff implications for both teams, the real intrigue is in everything around the game: Stuff like his relationship with the players who stayed at Ole Miss and an administration there that now feels conned by him, whether the atmosphere in Oxford is so toxic that it becomes dangerous and whether he would dare show up to his favorite hot yoga studio on Saturday morning.

But Kiffin is a case study in contradictions — well, either that or chronic phoniness. And with one obviously scripted comment Monday, he called into question the entire premise of why he left Ole Miss for the Bayou in the first place.

"I told the players today, man, you don't have anything to worry about as far as like attention on you all week. There's going to be so much attention and hatred and everything on me, I said, you just get to go play. Really, the pressure's on them. We won seven games last year, they won 13. They return two Heisman candidates. How often does that ever happen in the same backfield? We had it one time [at Southern Cal] with Matt Leinart and Reggie Bush . So you guys get to go play. The pressure's not on you."

If there is one thing we know for sure about why Kiffin left Ole Miss, it wasn't to be the underdog. Not in this game, not in any game.

Kiffin went to LSU to build the SEC's most feared and hated program, to work with an administration that does not care about personal accountability or competitive comity, to break norms and melt his competitors' brains over his willingness to operate in gray areas without a shred of regret.

He went there, not just to win, but to dominate — backed by a governor's mansion that sees him as a vehicle for its political ambitions and enabled by a university administration that would rather jump in Mike the Tiger's cage than tell their football coach no.

And now, on the eve of a game where he can show the world why going to LSU was the no-brainer move he believed it to be, here was Kiffin trying to play philosophy professor rather than the stone-cold killer LSU thought it paid $13 million a year for.

"In games, there's a winner and a loser, but sometimes in decisions and things that go on, there's not always a winner and a loser," he said. "They've been playing this matchup for a long time and this is the first time in the last 64 years both teams are in the top 10 … I think it's a really good thing that a lot of people could look at it and say, hey, both sides are doing really well and both sides won."

If Kiffin wants to be seen as anything other than a cartoon villain, he needs to get his story straight.

He wants so badly to be talked about as this longshot story who overcame doubts and setbacks, when in reality he was born into football privilege and got head coaching jobs at two blue-blood programs and the Oakland Raiders by the time he was 35 years old.

He wants to be viewed as the counterculture guy running afoul of the establishment when, in fact, nobody in college football history has been given more chances at great jobs despite massive amounts of self-sabotage.

He built a social media presence on being edgy and cool when, in person, he is awkward and introverted.

He has left a trail of burnt bridges everywhere he's been, but when it's time to account for it publicly, Kiffin always runs from the smoke.

What is real and what is fake with Lane? Depends whether he's coaching for or against you. Because Ole Miss doesn't get a pass, either. They aided and abetted all of it for six years and were ready to bend over backward for six more — until they realized Kiffin wasn't deciding whether to leave but rather just stalling for time before trying to take everything with him that wasn't nailed down.

The idea that "both sides won" is laughable gaslighting. It only turned out that way because Ole Miss refused to let Kiffin get everything he wanted.

And, hey, that's fine. College football is a brutal business. Kiffin made a decision to work for another school, which was his right, and tried to recruit all the best players at Ole Miss to join him — some of which did and some of which didn't. All of it was fair game.

It should work out pretty well for both sides this year, but only because Kiffin couldn't take QB Trinidad Chambliss and RB Kewan Lacy to Baton Rouge with him. But the idea that Kiffin was happy to settle for a "win-win" divorce is laughable because it simply isn't true.

Trying to pretend like it's all good now, five days before the game, would be like Kiffin dying his blond hair black and telling us we're the crazy ones for noticing.

People can accept that Kiffin did kind of a scummy thing by abandoning Ole Miss before the CFP. It's his life, his career and he's the one who will have to live with those regrets. College sports has forgiven coaches for much worse.

But what nobody should accept are his attempts to rewrite history, by offering reasons for leaving that he knows are bogus (like this summer's GQ article where he mentioned the dark history associated with Ole Miss) and trying to Eddie Haskell his way through this week as the protagonist in his own redemption story.

We all know who you are, Lane. On the eve of the biggest game you've ever coached — tactically fascinating, unusually relevant to the national championship picture and deeply personal for many players and coaches on both sides — just be that guy without the ill-fitting costume you tried to wear Monday.

Put on the black hat once and for all and own it. If not, what was the point of going to LSU in the first place?

articles.title: Farke hails ‘one of the best performances of past 12 months’ after Leeds thrash Newcastle
articles.summary: Daniel Farke hailed Leeds’ 4-1 win over Newcastle as one of their best performances of the past 12 months after his side extended their unbeaten start to the...
articles.body:
Daniel Farke hailed Leeds ' 4-1 win over Newcastle as one of their best performances of the past 12 months after his side extended their unbeaten start to the Premier League season.

Leeds were dominant against Newcastle as they claimed their first home league win of the campaign thanks to goals from Jayden Bogle , Dominic Calvert-Lewin , Noah Okafor and a Lewis Miley own goal.

Farke said the intensity and focus shown by his players had been evident throughout the opening weeks of the season.

"I was just aware that the boys were on it because we had an unbeaten start in the league and have played so, so well and wanted to extend this unbeaten start," he said.

"Obviously we had the chance to win the first home game and to get already to eight points and you could feel that everyone was really on it."

The Leeds boss insisted the display was not the result of any extra edge, pointing to the standards his side had already shown in training and in previous results.

"Even in the training weeks before they were on it, otherwise we wouldn't have away wins at Nottingham Forest or something like this," Farke added.

"So I wouldn't say there was an extra edge but performance-wise you have to give credit to them.

"It was one of the best performances, I think, over the last 12 months."
