articles.title: Londres busca nuevo 'rey' para el Balón de Oro
articles.standfirst: El 70 aniversario del premio se celebrará el 26 de octubre en Londres, en la edición más abierta de los últimos años, con varios candidatos y ningún favorito claro
articles.summary: El 70 aniversario del premio se celebrará el 26 de octubre en Londres, en la edición más abierta de los últimos años, con varios candidatos y ningún favorito claro
articles.body: El Balón de Oro cambia París por Londres para celebrar sus 70 años. El próximo lunes 26 de octubre, el teatro London Palladium acogerá la gala en la que se nombrará al 'rey' del fútbol en 2026. Será la primera vez desde 2015 que la ceremonia se celebra fuera de la capital francesa, después de que Zúrich acogiera las entregas de los galardones entre 2010 y 2015. La elección de Londres tiene un motivo especial. El premio cumple siete décadas y rendirá homenaje a su primer monarca: Sir Stanley Matthews. El inglés conquistó el Balón de Oro en su primera edición en 1956 con el Blackpool, por encima de Alfredo Di Stefano y Raymond Kopa. Lo hizo, además, con 41 años, siendo el jugador más veterano en lograrlo. El premio, coorganizado por France Football y la UEFA, mantendrá el formato implantado en los últimos años. Por quinta ocasión, los galardones tendrán en cuenta el rendimiento durante una temporada completa y no durante el año natural. En este caso, desde el 1 de agosto de 2025 hasta el 31 de julio de 2026. La edición llega, además, con un ingrediente que aumenta todavía más la expectación, pues es el Balón de Oro más abierto de los últimos años. Hay varios jugadores con argumentos para levantar el prestigioso trofeo y, a diferencia de otras ediciones, no existe un favorito claro que parta por encima del resto. La temporada ha dejado una nómina de candidatos muy amplia y la lucha se presenta más igualada que nunca. La selección española, campeona del mundo, cuenta con una amplia representación. Lamine Yamal, Rodri Hernández, Fabián Ruiz, Ferran Torres, Marc Cucurella y Pau Cubarsí forman parte de una lista en la que también destaca el peso del PSG campeón de Europa. El conjunto parisino aporta al propio Fabián, Ousmane Dembélé, Vitinha, William Pacho, Marquinhos, João Neves, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Nuno Mendes y Achraf Hakimi, además de Ferran, (recién fichado en el mercado estival) todos ellos protagonistas de la campaña que llevó al equipo francés a volver conquistar la Champions. Pero el abanico de candidatos no termina ahí. Kylian Mbappé, Michael Olise y Harry Kane, Lionel Messi (vuelve a estar nominado tras tres ediciones de ausencia) también figuran entre los grandes nombres de una lista a la que llegan después de firmar grandes campañas. A su vez, hay espacio para las sorpresas, como Julián Quiñones o Sadio Mané. Vinicius Júnior, Erling Haaland y Jude Bellingham completan el grupo de estrellas, aunque, a priori, con menos opciones de pelear por el oro. En el lado contrario, sorprenden las ausencias de Raphinha y Pedri entre los 30 nominados. Entre todos ellos, Ousmane Dembélé parte como vigente ganador. El atacante francés buscará revalidar un premio que se presenta más abierto que nunca, con varios candidatos y sin un favorito claro. La campaña por el Balón de Oro ya ha arrancado y Londres será el escenario de su desenlace. El próximo 26 de octubre, el mundo conocerá a su nuevo ganador.

articles.title: Leeds 4-1 Newcastle: Is 'unplayable' Calvert-Lewin in line for England recall?
articles.summary: Dominic Calvert-Lewin has now scored in Leeds' last five league matches. Is he ready for and England recall?
articles.body:
Newcastle United must be sick of the sight of Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

The Leeds United striker has now scored eight times against the club he was previously linked with in years gone by.

So you suspect the beleaguered visitors will have been a little relieved to see him substituted late on after he had a hand in two of Leeds ' goals in this impressive 4-1 win .

Elland Road was unsurprisingly on its feet to hand Calvert-Lewin a deserved standing ovation when he came off.

On a night Leeds fans repeatedly taunted Newcastle for spending "all that money" with little return on Monday night, at least, it was a free transfer who caused the visitors real problems with a goal and an assist.

So is the 29-year-old making a case for an England recall?

Leeds manager Daniel Farke certainly thinks so as he threw his weight behind Calvert-Lewin and a number of others in his side with "English passports".

"He's a handful and tough for each and every defender," he said.

"He's difficult to play against. He's at a top fitness level. You can see he plays with confidence and a good rhythm, but also benefits from a really strong team and players who work for him.

"Dominic is a crucial player and if he shows this type of form, he's definitely one of the best strikers in this league. It's the best league in the world and that more or less sums up what I think about him as a player."

Leeds move third as they hit four against Newcastle

Calvert-Lewin stars but Botman struggles - player ratings for Leeds v Newcastle

Calvert-Lewin has been in England head coach Thomas Tuchel's thoughts in recent months.

The striker was previously called up by his country back in March after catching the eye in his debut season at Leeds .

However, after featuring for England against Uruguay during that particular international window, the striker ultimately missed out on the World Cup in the summer.

Ivan Toney and Ollie Watkins instead travelled as captain Harry Kane's deputies.

At a time when the marginally older pair are both playing in Saudi Arabia, Calvert-Lewin is staking his claim with his performances closer to home in this country.

He has scored three goals in his past four games as the Premier League's leading English striker - just as Tuchel prepares to name his squad on Friday for the upcoming Nations League fixtures against Spain and the Czech Republic.

He is also just the second Leeds player to score in five consecutive Premier League appearances at Elland Road after Mark Viduka between March and August 2003.

Such was Calvert-Lewin's hunger, he looked dumbfounded after learning his header for Leeds ' second against Newcastle had been awarded to team-mate Jayden Bogle after it took a final touch off his team-mate.

Former England defender Jamie Carragher was among those watching on impressed following his "almost perfect" display.

"Maybe sometimes composure has let him down in his career, but not here," he told Sky Sports about the former Everton striker. "He was unplayable.

"It was right for him and Everton to make a fresh start. As an Evertonian you are probably thinking why didn't we keep him.

"Sometimes a move rejuvenates a player. He is the type of player you think as an ex-centre-back, I am glad I am not playing now."

Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?

No side will relish coming up against Calvert-Lewin and this aggressive Leeds outfit at Elland Road this season.

In fact, only Arsenal (52), Manchester City (50), Manchester United (45) and Bournemouth (37) have won more Premier League points in 2026 than Leeds United (35), with the Whites suffering just a single defeat across their past 13 league matches.

Yet Newcastle 's implosion was remarkable as a young team were bullied and outfought.

Newcastle had previously made a good start under head coach Matthias Jaissle, following so much change in the summer, and were unbeaten in their opening five games in all competitions before this reality check.

But they have faced more shots than any other side in the Premier League.

However clinical Newcastle were in the opening weeks of the campaign, they mustered just eight efforts on target against Liverpool , Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth before their trip to Elland Road.

That was a dangerous cocktail going into this game.

What was most galling, though, was the visitors' failure to match Leeds ' bite at a raucous Elland Road.

Jaissle's side crumbled and conceded three goals in a chastening 14-minute period in the first half.

It was a night the German manager swore in his post-match news conference to illustrate how low he felt.

"I don't want to point fingers and point any players out tonight," he said. "We were not matching as a team the level of intensity, the level of duel behaviours, the level of physicality.

"This is something we need to bring on the pitch in every match. This is non-negotiable. It should be the basic fundamentals of football.

"These are young lads. The learning curve needs to be fast."

For Calvert-Lewin and Leeds , however, this was a night to remember.

articles.title: Mike LaFleur aces head coaching debut with Cardinals, earning a win and some much-needed momentum
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals had one of their most encouraging Week 1 performances in years Sunday, entering as 9.5-point underdogs before beating the Los Angeles C...
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. (AP) — Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love looks like a keeper. So does first-year coach Mike LaFleur.

The Arizona Cardinals had one of their most encouraging Week 1 performances in years Sunday, entering as 9.5-point underdogs before beating the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 in a road victory that surprised just about everybody except for the players and coaches in the winning locker room.

"We're not dumb, it's not that we don't hear the noise," LaFleur said. "We just ignore the noise, be above the noise."

The 39-year-old LaFleur bucked a franchise trend by becoming the first non-interim coach to win his first game since Don Coryell did it with the then-St. Louis Cardinals in 1973. For a team that finished with a 3-14 record last season, the victory was a galvanizing moment and a sign this year might be much more competitive.

LaFleur received hearty hugs from owner Michael Bidwill and general manager Monti Ossenfort in the aftermath of Sunday's win. The jubilation wasn't just because the Cardinals had won a football game. It's that they beat what's supposed to be a really good Chargers team and looked competent on offense, defense and special teams.

Journeyman Jacoby Brissett completed 27 of 37 passes for 277 yards and a touchdown, providing a calm presence in the pocket that lived up to the $15.5 million, one-year reworked deal he signed at the beginning of training camp. All-Pro tight end Trey McBride caught nine passes for 95 yards and a touchdown and Love scored his first career touchdown, running five yards to give the Cardinals an early 7-0 lead.

But more than the superlatives, what's notable is there were not many negatives.

The offensive line protected well, the much-maligned defense was effective and Simi Fehoko had an important special teams moment, blocking a punt in the fourth quarter that set up a touchdown and put the game out of reach.

Nobody's calling the Cardinals Super Bowl contenders, but there's suddenly lots of optimism for a franchise that hasn't had much of it recently.

Arizona 's defense was one of the worst in the NFL last season and still a huge question mark heading into Week 1 this year, but performed better than expected. Linebacker Mack Wilson Sr.'s hard hit on Chargers receiver Ladd McConkey , safety Andrew Wingard 's interception and a split sack for Budda Baker and Jack Gibbens in the fourth quarter were among the big moments.

Defensive coordinator Nick Rallis — one of the holdovers from Jonathan Gannon's staff last season — wasn't fazed after the Cardinals gave up a touchdown on the opening drive. Instead, he made adjustments and the Cardinals held the Chargers' offense to 268 yards.

The Cardinals weren't great in the red zone, scoring touchdowns on just two of five opportunities.

"Wasn't thrilled with the red zone plan and it starts with me," LaFleur said. "You kick too many field goals in this league and more times than not you'll get beat."

Love's 41 yards rushing on 11 carries might not jump off the stat sheet, but the No. 3 overall pick out of Notre Dame still looked the part of a future star.

The 21-year-old showed creativity on his 5-yard TD run, bouncing to the outside on a play designed to go up the middle, and had several other hard-nosed runs where he gained at least a few yards after there appeared to be no running room.

"I mean the touchdown was all him," Brissett said. "I don't think he was supposed to go that way. But the way he handled the ball, I was like, 'Oh, OK yeah' and I thought he played well in the pass and run game."

It was a quiet day for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and defensive lineman Walter Nolen III , two young cornerstones that the Cardinals hope will have big seasons.

Harrison did make a fantastic 33-yard catch, but that was his only reception. Nolen drew a lot of attention from the Chargers' offensive line and finished with just one tackle.

The Cardinals came out of the game mostly unscathed though cornerback Max Melton and safety Kitan Crawford are dealing with ankle injuries.

13 — Brissett has thrown for at least 200 yards and one touchdown in 13 straight starts, breaking the franchise record of 12 set by Kurt Warner over the 2008-09 seasons.

The Cardinals have another tough game when the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks visit on Sunday.

articles.title: Penn State DT gives heartbreaking explanation for continuing CFB
articles.summary: Penn State defensive tackle Siale Taupaki is in his eight year of college football, but he has a heartbreaking reason for why.
articles.body:
Penn State defensive tackle Siale Taupaki might be one of the last people you think of when you list players on the defense, but he'll be getting all the shine this week. He is presumably in his last year of college football with this being his eighth season on a roster, and he recently revealed why it's so important for him to play.

When Taupaki was asked why playing for Penn State is such an important opportunity for him, he told reporters, "My parents are still struggling, you know, I'm broke. So, while everybody else is still trying to buy their next pendant or buy their next car, I'm really just trying to fill in all the holes that I have back at home."

It was an eye-opening statement from the man who's had one of the strangest journeys ever through college football. He began his collegiate career in 2019, but with the COVID-19 season and countless redshirts, Taupaki barely saw the field in his first few seasons. He finally registered his first statistic in 2024 with the UCLA Bruins , and now he'll finish out his career with the Nittany Lions .

Some of these players who get extended eligibility and play into their mid-20s are ridiculed by fans, but Taupaki's situation shows exactly why it's not always just a shameless cash grab. These are real people who have struggles just like everyone else, and some of them desperately need NIL money to provide for their families.

Taupaki has flown under the radar as an athlete, but he made somewhat of a name for himself with his comments last week. He'll be a player to look for the rest of the season because his press conference made it impossible not to root for him.

articles.title: Bills, Jets the two AFC East teams to win in Week 1
articles.summary: Taking a look at the AFC East standings through one week
articles.body:
As week 1 comes to a close in the National Football League, we got to see an early look on what the AFC East may look like throughout the season. After their first games of the season the standings are as follows:

The Bills were finally able to pick up a win in Houston for the first time since 2006. For Josh Allen it marked his first win in that stadium and he had to earn it that's for sure. Allen finished the day with 334 passing yards with two touchdowns through the air and another two touchdowns on the ground. It was not a pleasant day for the defense allowing 31 points but shoutout to Deone Walker and Greg Rousseau for clutch sacks on the last drive of the game to clinch the victory.

New York got themselves a road victory as well to start the season in the Robert Saleh Bowl defeating the Tennessee Titans . Who knows what the expectations are for the Jets but after one week there could be some hope. Geno Smith had a productive day at quarterback with no turnovers, and Breece Hall had a 100 yard rushing performance with a touchdown. This is a big season for coach Aaron Glenn because another bad season will likely lead to a new head coach for Gang Green while the team hopefully drafts their quarterback of the future.

The Patriots lost and Bills fans can point to the reason being that they played a "real opponent," but I would be quick to hold that judgement. Remember a couple seasons ago, Josh Allen threw away a game against the Jets to open the season with silly interceptions giving a victory to Zach Wilson . The same can be said about Drake Maye who was in control for the majority of the game until a string of three fourth-quarter picks. New England showed that they still have a great defense so they can still prove themselves to be contenders again this season. The issue will be that the talk of the offseason was that the team needed a number one receiver. After finally getting one in AJ Brown , he finds himself on IR with a high ankle sprain and will most likely miss six games according to reports.

Lastly with the Dolphins, this marked the beginning of the Malik Willis era at quarterback. Willis showed off the big arm at times but also showed some poor decision making throwing an interception and taking some sacks that could have been avoided. Running back De'Von Achane was held to only 36 rushing yards which is not the recipe for success for Miami. The defense did force a couple of interceptions from Kirk Cousins but could not stop Ashton Jeanty who had 100 yards rushing and two touchdowns as a receiver.

articles.standfirst: El centrocampista explica los motivos de su fichaje por el Barça en 'Mundo Deportivo'
articles.summary: El centrocampista explica los motivos de su fichaje por el Barça en 'Mundo Deportivo'
articles.body: Rodrigo Hernández desvela en una entrevista en Mundo Deportivo lo ocurrido el pasado verano. El capitán de la selección explica los motivos por los que eligió fichar por el Barcelona, rechazando para ello la propuesta que recibió del Real Madrid. Rodri asegura que su elección se debió a criterios futbolísticos: "Hubo que analizar muchas cosas y tomar una decisión tan importante con dos de los mejores clubs del mundo. Al final tomé una decisión por el plano deportivo, por lo que me suscitaba un poquito más de ganas y de entender dónde podía ganar y crecer más como jugador. No fue una decisión fácil para nada, decir que no al Madrid no es fácil y sobre todo que tuvieron un comportamiento ejemplar conmigo". En la entrevista, Rodri también tiene buenas palabras para Mourinho, quien telefoneó incluso al jugador para darle a conocer sus intenciones: "El trato fue muy bueno. Cuando tomé la decisión también le llamé para agradecer el interés y el trato. Me parece un grandísimo entrenador, ya lo ha demostrado allá donde ha ido en sus grandes etapas y el Real Madrid va a ser un duro rival para esta Liga". Las figuras de Deco y Flick tuvieron un papel clave en la decisión del 16 azulgrana: "Me gustó mucho la manera de tratar y no ir con esa ansiedad del Barça. Y sobre todo la naturalidad con la que me lo hicieron saber. Fue una sensación muy familiar, de club familiar, y eso me atrajo mucho. No fue un tema de intentar convencerte con números, no. Fue más un tema futbolístico, de lo que entendían que podía aportar dentro y fuera del campo".

articles.title: Louisiana governor hopes for 'Southern hospitality' when Lane Kiffin returns to Ole Miss with LSU
articles.summary: Governor Jeff Landry joked about using military aircraft to transport Kiffin and the LSU team to Oxford before Saturday's highly charged matchup with Ole Mis...
articles.body:
LSU visiting Ole Miss would likely have been considered the top matchup for Week 3 of the college football season with the Tigers ranked No. 7 and the Rebels right behind them at No. 8 in the AP Top 25 poll .

But Saturday's game also comes with a significant dose of intrigue and potential drama with Lane Kiffin returning to Oxford, Mississippi after leaving Ole Miss for LSU before the end of last season .

How Kiffin will be greeted by Rebels fans is the great question leading up to Saturday night's SEC clash. Some are even concerned that the tensions could get out of hand with outraged fans wanting to lash out at Kiffin.

Included among those is Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry. Well, sort of. While he acknowledged that feelings will surely be heightened, the governor joked about what measures might be necessary to ensure the safety of Kiffin and the LSU football team .

"I'm thinking about having to send him in on an F-16 and maybe the team on a C-130," Landry said to ESPN's Mark Schlabach . "Security is going to be really tight. You know, we might need the National Guard out there to protect our team. I think it's going to be an interesting weekend."

Presumably on a more serious note. Landry added that he's spoken with officials at Ole Miss to ensure that the atmosphere in and around Oxford's Vaught–Hemingway Stadium is safe for LSU.

"I know that we've been talking with Mississippi and making sure that we have adequate security for the team and coach," Landry continued. "But I'm hoping that we can go there and play in complete Southern hospitality and have a great, great game."

Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding, who was the Rebels' defensive coordinator before Kiffin left for LSU, also pleaded for calm and reason from fans on Saturday.

"Be there early and be loud," Golding said at his weekly press conference . "That's the one thing to me about Oxford, the first thing you talk about is the people there. Let's not lose that over a game, over a person or anything else like that." "There's nothing wrong with being competitive, being in the moment, being really loud and being an unbelievable fan," he added. "At the end of the day, don't lose what we've created. And what they've created for so long, which is a unique place with really, really good people where it's really hard to play."
